key_insight: A locality-preserving Derby-Klassen fermion-to-qubit mapping, combined with constraint-aware HVA/VQE, can simulate interacting 2D fermionic models with shorter Pauli strings and better access to symmetry sectors than Jordan-Wigner circuits.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to reduce circuit depth and operator nonlocality for quantum simulation of higher-dimensional materials and many-body models on near-term hardware.
method: Use the DK mapping to keep fermionic interactions local in qubit space while adding auxiliary constraints for the physical subspace.
Prepare constrained states with Clifford gates and embed them in a Hamiltonian Variational Ansatz.
Run VQE while exploiting particle-number conservation to target different symmetry sectors and compare against Jordan-Wigner circuits at nonzero chemical potential.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that low-energy properties are accurately reproduced for 2D t-V and Fermi-Hubbard models, including degenerate states and cases where Jordan-Wigner becomes less favorable at nonzero chemical potential.
watch_item: The DK approach introduces extra qubits and stabilizer/constraint-preparation overhead, so the net advantage depends on whether reduced nonlocality outweighs this added implementation cost.
paper_title: Investigating Interacting Fermionic Models with Locality-Preserving Qubit Encodings
